paragraphs: He is mentioned in the old Midrash Tehillim, 106, chapter 106; Hyman says the reading should be Rabbi Huna HaKohen, as in Buber’s Midrash Tehillim.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The supplied “106, chapter 106” repetition is retained. The OYW digital Midrash Tehillim 106 text fully writes Rabbi Huna HaKohen, supporting that name form. This comparison does not inspect Buber’s printed edition or his editorial annotation.

The whole OYW Midrash Tehillim 106 paragraph fully writes Rabbi Huna HaKohen in a chain with abbreviated R' Yirmeya and R' Chiyya HaGadol. This supports Hyman’s proposed Huna form, without supplying a full title for the differing Yehudah heading, rendered R'. His repeated 106/chapter 106 and his Buber report remain intact; no fresh printed-edition collation, title transfer or identity merge is claimed.
